arxiv-2103-16077.title: Parameterized discrete uniformization theorems and curvature flows for polyhedral surfaces, II
arxiv-2103-16077.creator: Xu Xu, Chao Zheng
arxiv-2103-16077.description: Abstract This paper investigates the combinatorial α \alpha -curvature for vertex scaling of piecewise hyperbolic metrics on polyhedral surfaces, which is a parameterized generalization of the classical combinatorial curvature. A discrete uniformization theorem for combinatorial α \alpha -curvature is established, which generalizes Gu-Guo-Luo-Sun-Wu’s discrete uniformization theorem for classical combinatorial curvature [ 16 ] .

arxiv-2109-07693.title: High order harmonic generation in semiconductors driven at near- and mid-IR wavelengths
arxiv-2109-07693.creator: David Freeman, Shunsuke Yamada, Atsushi Yamada, Anatoli Kheifets, Kazuhiro Yabana
arxiv-2109-07693.description: Abstract We study high order harmonics generation (HHG) in crystalline silicon and diamond subjected to near and mid-infrared laser pulses. We employ time-dependent density functional theory and solve the time-dependent Kohn-Sham equation in the single-cell geometry. We demonstrate that clear and clean HHG spectra can be generated with careful selection of the pulse duration.

arxiv-2204-12208.title: An electronic origin of charge order in infinite-layer nickelates
arxiv-2204-12208.creator: Hanghui Chen, Yi-feng Yang, Guang-Ming Zhang, Hongquan Liu
arxiv-2204-12208.description: Abstract A charge order (CO) with a wavevector 𝐪 ≃ ( 1 3 , 0 , 0 ) \mathbf{q}\simeq\left(\frac{1}{3},0,0\right) is observed in infinite-layer nickelates. Here we use first-principles calculations to demonstrate a charge-transfer-driven CO mechanism in infinite-layer nickelates, which leads to a characteristic Ni 1+ -Ni 2+ -Ni 1+ stripe state.

arxiv-2310-05787.title: Exact threshold for approximate ellipsoid fitting of random points
arxiv-2310-05787.creator: Antoine Maillard, Afonso S. Bandeira
arxiv-2310-05787.description: Abstract We consider the problem ( P ) (\rm P) of exactly fitting an ellipsoid (centered at 0 0 ) to n n standard Gaussian random vectors in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , as n , d → ∞ n,d\to\infty with n / d 2 → α > 0 n/d^{2}\to\alpha>0 .

arxiv-2311-09166.title: Optimizing Fictitious States for Bell Inequality Violation in Bipartite Qubit Systems with Applications to the t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} System
arxiv-2311-09166.creator: Kun Cheng, Tao Han, Matthew Low
arxiv-2311-09166.description: Abstract There is a significant interest in testing quantum entanglement and Bell inequality violation in high-energy experiments. Since the analyses in high-energy experiments are performed with events statistically averaged over phase space, the states used to determine observables depend on the choice of coordinates through an event-dependent basis and are thus not genuine quantum states, but rather “fictitious states.

arxiv-2402-15018.title: Unintended Impacts of LLM Alignment on Global Representation
arxiv-2402-15018.creator: Michael J. Ryan, William Held, Diyi Yang
arxiv-2402-15018.description: Abstract Before being deployed for user-facing applications, developers align Large Language Models (LLMs) to user preferences through a variety of procedures, such as Reinforcement Learning From Human Feedback (RLHF) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Current evaluations of these procedures focus on benchmarks of instruction following, reasoning, and truthfulness.

arxiv-2601-01018.title: Spatially-Coupled Network RNA Velocities: A Control-Theoretic Perspective
arxiv-2601-01018.creator: Boya Hou, Maxim Raginsky, Abhishek Pandey, Olgica Milenkovic
arxiv-2601-01018.description: Abstract RNA velocity is an important model that combines cellular spliced and unspliced RNA counts to infer dynamical properties of various regulatory functions. Despite its wide applicability and many variants used in practice, the model has not been adequately designed to directly account for both intracellular gene regulatory network interactions and spatial intercellular communications.

pmc-10480159.title: CRISPR imaging reveals chromatin fluctuation at the centromere region related to cellular senescence
pmc-10480159.creator: Hideaki Takata, Yumena Masuda, Nobuko Ohmido
pmc-10480159.description: The human genome is spatially and temporally organized in the nucleus as chromatin, and the dynamic structure of chromatin is closely related to genome functions. Cellular senescence characterized by an irreversible arrest of proliferation is accompanied by chromatin reorganisation in the nucleus during senescence. However, chromatin dynamics in chromatin reorganisation is poorly understood.

pmc-11378893.title: DNA metabarcoding unveils the hidden species composition in fish surimi: Implications for the management of unlabeled and mixed seafood products
pmc-11378893.creator: Hung-Tai Lee, Cheng-Hsin Liao, Te-Hua Hsu
pmc-11378893.description: Fish surimi products are traditional foods primarily made from fish meat and may contain a complex species composition. In Taiwan, the abundant fishery resources and diverse fish species lead to local catches being widely used as ingredients in fish surimi products.

pmc-11438005.title: Changes in soft tissue dimensions following horizontal guided bone regeneration with a split-thickness flap design – evaluation of 8 cases with a digital method
pmc-11438005.creator: Kristof Somodi, Andrea Dobos, Ferenc Bartha, Eleonora Solyom, Peter Windisch, Daniel Palkovics, Balint Molnar
pmc-11438005.description: BackgroundPeri-implant soft tissue corrections are often indicated following alveolar ridge augmentation, due to the distortion of the keratinized mucosa at the area of augmentation. The objective of the current study was to evaluate the dimensional soft tissue changes following horizontal guided bone regeneration (GBR) utilizing 3D digital data.

pmc-11610539.title: ‘Endless variation on a theme’: a document analysis of international and UK major trauma triage tools
pmc-11610539.creator: Gordon Fuller, Chris Holt, Samuel Keating, Janette Turner, MATTS research group contributors
pmc-11610539.description: Introduction:Triage tools are used within trauma networks to identify which injured patients should be bypassed and pre-alerted to major trauma centres. Despite the importance of treating the ‘right patient in the right place at the right time’, there has been no consensus on triage tool structure or content.

pmc-12417588.title: Exploring the Needs and Preferences of Patients with Port-Wine Stain and Associated Syndromes: A Qualitative Analysis of Social Media Discussions
pmc-12417588.creator: Yichen Liu, Xu Liu, Min-Kyu Kim, Beenu Maharjan, Xinjin Liu, Yuxin Duan, Dingling Li, Long Lin, Jingyuan Zeng, Hanfei Qin, Yifei Cheng, Linghong Guo, Xian Jiang
pmc-12417588.description: PurposePatients with port-wine stain (PWS) and related syndromes often face multifaceted challenges in disease management, including prolonged treatment cycles, appearance-related distress, and psychological burdens. Social media has become an important platform for these individuals to obtain information and share experiences. However, there is a lack of systematic qualitative research exploring their genuine needs.

pmc-12595985.title: High Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion (HSIL) Positive Disease Risk Nomogram Model: A Single Centre Retrospective Analysis
pmc-12595985.creator: Qiu-Zhen Wu, Mao-Hua Lin, Jian-Rui Zheng, Xiu-Qing Weng, Li-Li Zheng, Ying-Yu Mao
pmc-12595985.description: PurposeTo develop and validate a nomogram for predicting high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions or worse (HSIL+), incorporating results from ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) and Aptima HPV E6/E7 mRNA (AHPV) testing.Patients and MethodsThis diagnostic study consecutively enrolled 3,202 patients referred for colposcopy due to abnormal cervical screening results.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— The Secretary shall furnish to former members of the Armed Forces described in subsection (b)— (1) an initial mental health assessment; and (2).
